characteristic_audit: All multiplicities are defined through graph-ideal powers, equivalently normal Hasse jets. No factorial or ordinary derivative is divided by.
The theorem assumes D<p. Hence every positive Z-exponent is below p, so a Z-dependent interpolant has nonzero formal Z-derivative and polynomial-function aliasing such as t^p-t cannot occur.
For genuine order s>=2 vanishing, every first derivative vanishes on each constrained graph. Global squarefreeness or a globally nonzero discriminant does not restore the simple-root condition there.
No irreducibility or absolute-irreducibility hypothesis is used. The example Y^2+Z^2 is only used as an F_103-irreducible, squarefree example.
Content division is audited explicitly: it may reduce graph multiplicity, as A=YZ and A/Y=Z demonstrate.

Adapted affine coordinates handle vertical lines without slope division. Repeated lines are deduplicated, parallel lines contribute no intersection root, and concurrent witnesses at one point do not contribute additive multiplicity.
If d>p/2 and D<p, primitive multiplicity s>=2 is impossible because D>=sd.
The inseparable example Z^p-X shows why d
counterexample_attempts: Ordinary graph vanishing does not transfer multiplicity: at p=103,d=101, A=Z vanishes on M(t)=(t,0), P_M=0, but restricts to t on L(t)=(0,t), P_L=t.
Vertical Z-Hasse conditions alone are insufficient: A=X+Z^s has its Z-Hasse derivatives of orders below s vanishing on X=Z=0, yet can have a simple transverse restriction.
Content removal destroys multiplicity: A=YZ lies in (Y,Z)^2 and is squarefree with weighted degree 102<103, but its primitive part Z does not lie in (Y,Z)^2.
Squarefree and irreducible do not imply a simple root along the graph: over F_103, A=Y^2+Z^2 is squarefree and irreducible, yet all first derivatives vanish on Y=Z=0.
Inseparability beyond D<p: B=Z^p-X is absolutely irreducible and smooth but B_Z=0; B(t,t)=t^p-t vanishes at every field element without being the zero polynomial.

Concentrated directions: with f=0, P_L=0 in k directions and P_L=1 otherwise, epsilon=k/(p+1) and every point has exactly k accepting lines. This realizes the Cauchy-Schwarz squaring loss but has global polynomial Q=0, so it is not a soundness counterexample.

For arbitrary f, each line polynomial can interpolate d+1 chosen values, giving local agreement at least (d+1)/p. This confirms the natural d/p floor but does not contradict a theorem with a sufficiently large threshold constant.

finite_sanity_checks: At p=103,d=101, direct modular evaluation verified that A=Z has one transverse root, while YZ and Y^2+Z^2 have a double transverse root and zero gradient on the selected graph.
For p=103, -1 is a nonsquare, so Y^2+Z^2 is F_103-irreducible and squarefree; its weighted degree is 2d=202>p.
The exact counts at d=101,D=202,s=2 are N_d(D)=25960 and C_s(D,d)=507, matching the closed formula.

At p=103,d=101, the total-degree code dimension is 5253, so a triangular information set gives every point table agreement at least 5253/103^2, approximately 0.495. Thus the near-p case is a method limitation, not a theorem counterexample.

A separate arithmetic check with prime p=1000000007 and d=101 gave identical conservative normalized degree D/s=50848800 for s=1,2,4, confirming the predicted cancellation. This is only a sanity check, not an asymptotic proof.
global_conclusion: A fully quantified transverse-jet interpolation lemma and a rigorous architecture-specific obstruction were proved. Uniform higher multiplicity cannot improve the cubic exponent when existence is certified by raw coefficient-versus-jet counting and propagation is certified by univariate root multiplicity. The result neither improves nor refutes the bivariate soundness benchmark. The only final global-agreement guarantee remains the quoted KTZ conclusion, at least epsilon/8000 in its m=2 proof.

obstructions: Uniform graph multiplicity has quadratic normal-jet cost but only linear root-multiplicity benefit.
The rank-blind coefficient-versus-equation architecture forces h^2>dn/12, independent of multiplicity.
Order at least two makes all first derivatives vanish along selected graphs, conflicting with simple-root Newton-Hensel lifting.
Squarefree reduction and content division preserve ordinary zero sets but not higher-order graph vanishing.
Under D<p, primitive multiplicity s requires D>=sd; hence no s>=2 is available when d>p/2.
Ordinary value consistency supplies no derivative or jet compatibility across an accepted intersection.

For the new lemma: distinct selected lines R of size n, uniform integer multiplicity s>=1, weighted degree d<=D<p, and h distinct compatible intersections on a target line. proof_steps.proof: Choose adapted affine coordinates (T,S,W) with the lifted graph ideal (S,W). The substitution is a filtered automorphism for weights 1,1,d.
proof_steps.statement: Every lifted line graph has characteristic-safe normal coordinates preserving weighted degree.

proof_steps.proof: Expanding A as sum c_ab(T)S^aW^b, membership in (S,W)^s is equivalent to c_ab=0 for a+b<s. Since deg c_ab<=D-a-db, the exact one-line codimension is C_s(D,d).
proof_steps.statement: Order-s graph vanishing costs exactly C_s(D,d) normal-jet channels on one line and at most nC_s across n lines.

proof_steps.proof: The weighted-degree-D space has N_d(D) coefficients. If N_d(D)>nC_s(D,d), homogeneous linear algebra gives a nonzero common jet interpolant.
proof_steps.statement: The coefficient-versus-jet inequality suffices for interpolation.

proof_steps.proof: A Z-independent solution is divisible by the s-th power of every distinct line equation, so D>=sn. More generally, if deg_Z A=z<s, then each line equation occurs to power s-z; n>D forces z>=s and D>=sd. With D<p, any Z-dependent A has A_Z nonzero.
proof_steps.statement: Nontrivial Z-dependence and the primitive degree cost are fully quantified.

proof_steps.proof: At a compatible transverse intersection, both normal generators vanish to order at least one on the target graph. Every element of the s-th ideal power therefore pulls back to a multiple of (t-t_0)^s.
proof_steps.statement: Full normal multiplicity transfers an s-fold root across one compatible intersection.

proof_steps.proof: The h intersection parameters are distinct, the restricted polynomial has degree at most D, and the product of their s-th powers divides it. Thus sh>D forces the restriction to vanish identically.
proof_steps.statement: Multiplicity root counting transfers the relation to a target line.

proof_steps.proof: N_d(D)>D^3/(16d) and C_s(D,d)<=s(s+1)D for D>=d. Hence D_0=floor(4sqrt(dns(s+1)))+1 suffices; D_0<sh completes transfer.
proof_steps.statement: An explicit finite-field interpolation-and-transfer parameter choice is valid.

proof_steps.proof: When n>D, D>=sd and C_s(D,d)>=s^2D/6, while N_d(D)<=2D^3/d. The raw dimension inequality implies D^2>dns^2/12; sh>D then implies h^2>dn/12. Substitution of n=Theta(p/epsilon), h=Theta(epsilon p) yields epsilon^3=Omega(d/p).
proof_steps.statement: Uniform multiplicity is exponent-neutral in the rank-blind KTZ interpolation/root-count architecture.

sampling_model: Choose L uniformly from the p(p+1) unparameterized affine lines of F_p^2, then choose x uniformly from the p points of L; equivalently, sample a uniform point-line incidence.
